title: Synthesized on-call brief composer (top spans, timeline, Slack approval)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: On-call responders currently receive large volumes of raw alerts and traces. Engineers waste time triaging noisy signals before they can understand causal spans and next steps. We need a compact, human-readable on-call brief that synthesizes the causal timeline, top latency/error spans, related metrics/log slices, and a draft postmortem skeleton, and then routes it through a light human-in-loop Slack approval before creating a postmortem and attaching runbook snippets.

Proposal: Build 'brief-composer' service that listens to incident events (PagerDuty alerts, ops webhook), queries the tracing store and metrics/log pipelines for the 30 minutes around the alert, extracts the top 5 spans by cumulative added latency and the top error clusters, generates a 6-8 line timeline with key metric deltas, attaches the canonical runbook snippet (from /runbooks/library v2) relevant to the service, and drafts a postmortem skeleton with prefilled hypothesis, impact, timeline, and remediation bullets. Before finalizing, open a Slack modal to the primary on-call for quick edits/approval; once approved, create the postmortem doc and add links to the incident and invoke a retention tagging step.

Goals: reduce mean time to initial understanding (MTIU) for incidents by 30%, lower noisy-followup pager escalations, and seed postmortems with useful structure to speed RCA.
acceptance_criteria: Brief is generated within 90s of incident creation for high-priority incidents
Top 5 spans are selected and include at least one KV or network span when present
Slack modal surfaces editable timeline + runbook snippet and requires explicit approve/decline
Approved brief creates a postmortem draft in Confluence with links to traces, dashboard slices, and PR template
Metric: MTIU for test incidents decreases in canary group by >=30% over baseline
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Event ingestion - wire PagerDuty -> brief-composer via existing alert bus (3 days)
Phase 2: Tracing inference - implement top-span selector using cumulative latency heuristics and service boundary scoring (5 days)
Phase 3: Metrics/log query templates - add pipeline queries to surface error clusters and metric deltas (4 days)
Phase 4: Slack approval flow - Slack modal + lightweight editor, tie to PD responder identity (3 days)
Phase 5: Postmortem scaffold generation and Confluence API integration (2 days)
Phase 6: Canary rollout to infra-oncall team, measure MTIU and gather qualitative feedback (7 days)
progress_updates: 2026-03-09: Kickoff meeting with Observability, Oncall, and Docs. Agreed on top-5 spans definition and required fields for brief.
2026-03-10: Prototype top-span selector implemented in a local notebook; initial algorithm: cumulative_duration * (error_count + 1) / span_count.
2026-03-11: Created Confluence PRD: https://rwd.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/BR-314159-brief-composer. Added sample brief templates.
2026-03-12: Opened implementation spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4920 (tracing query + selector). Reviewing with tracing team.
2026-03-13: Slack modal UX draft ready; design feedback from Elena Novak specifies inline edit and small-footprint summary only. Backend schema for brief saved to S3 draft-buckets agreed.
Next: implement metric slices and wire PagerDuty ack hook to trigger Slack modal in staging.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Human-in-loop vs fully automated postmortem creation: chose human-in-loop to avoid noisy/incorrect postmortems and to comply with sensitive-PII checks.

Top-5 span heuristic uses cumulative latency rather than largest single span to capture amplified fanout regressions; this may miss single catastrophic spans but improves signal for distributed bottlenecks.
We will store drafts in customer-owned buckets for Private deployments to avoid cross-tenant data leakage. Hosted will use encrypted internal storage with KMS keys.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Slack modal approval could be ignored and delay postmortems. Mitigation: add fallback auto-create after configurable grace period and notify incident commander.
Risk: Tracing queries could be expensive on large traces. Mitigation: sampling window (default 30m) and downsampling policy; run heavy queries off-hours for long-tail analysis.
Risk: Incorrect runbook snippet attachment. Mitigation: runbook versioning + confidence score; show source link in modal for reviewer sanity check.
testing_and_rollout: Unit tests for selector heuristics and metrics queries
Integration tests using synthetic traces (devtools/trace-faker) and an incident replay harness
Canary: enable for infra-oncall team on staging first, collect MTIU and qualitative feedback for 2 weeks
Rollout gating: MTIU improvement >=20% in canary and no false positives in runbook attachments
